COMPONENT KIT

  • Liquid-chrome type — gradient-clipped Manrope 800 with a dark horizon band and drop shadow
  • Jelly window — translucent candy-teal panel with white rim and soft teal shadow
  • Gel capsule — Aqua-style pill with a glossy top highlight — teal ok, coral alert, white secondary
  • Chrome blob — radial metallic blob that holds the Acme mark in a gel bubble
  • Pinstripes — 3 px white horizontal lines over an icy gradient background
  • Sparkles — 4-point stars that twinkle on the hi-hats

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Gel inflate — scale 0.6→1.08→1 with elastic.out(1, .6) 0.5 s — one beat at 120 BPM
  • Chrome glint — a white 30° highlight band sweeps across the lettering, sine.inOut 0.6 s, on beat 1 of each bar
  • Jelly wobble — scaleX/scaleY counter-oscillate ±4 %, 0.25 s per cycle on 8th notes, decaying over 2 beats

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Y2K chrome and gel are having a strong revival, so the look feels both nostalgic and current, and the translucent materials make a background agent feel light and friendly. Risk: gradients and glows can look cheap or muddy after compression; keep the palette tight (teal, coral, chrome) and the data on opaque capsules.

Adapt to your product: Rebuild your key UI states as gel capsules and jelly windows (status pills are perfect), and render your product name in liquid chrome for the reveal. Keep your real data flat and legible inside them.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y2K_aesthetic — Y2K aesthetic: chrome, translucent plastics, blobjects, late 1990s–2000s · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aqua_(user_interface) — Aqua (2000): gel buttons, translucency, 'lickable' UI
